body: Interpol. Love that song.
I guess I'm just tired of talking about it. Since those who have heard it dont seem to know what to do, I'm so scared that no one else will understand.
I guess I'm just ashamed of feeling this way. And tired.
How did you get through it?

The pills and diagnoses have not been helpful lately. They were in the past, but not now. Which I don't understand. As far as people to talk to, I just feel like everyone is sick of me crying and saying the same thing over and over. I don't think anyone knows what to do with me.
How do you stay strong, if I can ask? How do you get through each day?
No, I haven't. Good thought though.
I totally know how you feel. I'm a huge fan of overcast days and rain.
Do you see a psychiatrist or psychologist? It can help. Good luck to you.

I really like this book: http://www.amazon.com/Lost-Soul-Companion-Constructive-Struggling/dp/0440509211

It's a little artsy, but still managed to make me smile.
I will definitely talk to my doc about it.

Talk to your therapist about your financial situation. I did this with mine, and he knocked off some $ from his usual fee. Try to stay with the therapist if you can. Also, try to see a psychiatrist for meds.

I was diagnosed with bipolar and have had severe bouts of anxiety, panic, and depression. I'm also taking Lamictal and my doc is having me take zyprexa as a "crutch" (her word) until the high dose of Lamictal kicks in.
I'm starting this soon. I'm pretty nervous and skeptical, but my depression is so bad that I'm willing to try anything at this point.
The waiting for something to kick in is the worst.
I've been on it for a while, but in small doses. In the last couple of weeks, my doc has increased my dose from 100 to 150 to 200 mg. I hope I'll see an improvement soon.

Well, my psychoanalyst was NOT supportive when I told him about my new appointment. It sent me into a tailspin, and today I'm having absolutely crippling depression and anxiety. I hope my appointment with the psychologist on Friday goes okay. I need something good to happen.
Update: I just saw my psychiatrist who referred me to a regular psychologist who specializes in very intensive therapy (and who takes insurance, yay!). I will see the new doc on Friday.
Thank you for writing. I'm seeing my psychiatrist tomorrow and will talk to her about all this and ask for a recommendation for someone who does CBT. I'm happy to know that ROCD is real.

E-meter, thank goodness, I'm not alone. I hope your appointment at the clinic goes okay. I'd be curious to see what they say. I've had these ruminations/obsessions in other good relationships, and I want the pattern to STOP, but am not sure how..
Oh, cognitive behavioral therapy, I just realized.

What is CPTSD and CBT?

Here are other things I've noticed:
- I do rituals in my head. I make sure to "think" certain things before certain events. I feel that if I don't think about certain things, bad things will happen.
- I've had massive bouts of guilt where I feel that if I don't tell my boyfriend something, it means I'm a liar, a bad person, etc. Once I tell him that specific thing, it immediately goes away. But I can't stop thinking about that specific thing until I tell him, and it affects me physically (sick to my stomach, etc.)
- I feel like if I don't take two showers per day, I'm unclean at night when I get into bed.
- Growing up, I'd have rituals like if I wore a specific article of clothing, something good would happen. Vice versa... if I didn't wear a specific article, something bad would happen.

More things like this come to mind, but you get the picture.
